sections.text: I will tell thee now, O Mighty Man, the five causes which, according to the final decision of philosophy, must concur before an action can be accomplished.
अधिष्ठानं तथा कर्ता करणं च पृथग्विधम्।
They are a body, a personality, physical organs, their manifold activity and destiny.
Whatever action a man performs, whether by muscular effort or by speech or by thought, and whether it be right or wrong, these five are the essential causes.

We had been discussing Chapter 18, Moksha Sannyasa Yoga -- Yoga of Liberation through Renunciation. We are at the end of Bhagavad Gita. We have discussed 17 chapters. This is like making a work plan for ourselves. What is work strategy?
Work strategy is capabilities plus opportunity. So weve seen our capabilities in chapter two: that this self is indestructible, only the body is destructible. And then we have seen what our opportunities are. If we can align with that supreme self -- versus identifying with this limited being called the Ego, this body, mind and intellect -- then I have a chance to achieve my goal of perennial happiness, unlimited happiness. Right now, because I am identified with this limited self, my happiness is also limited. There are limited capabilities, limited opportunities, therefore limited outcomes.
But I do have an opportunity to align myself with the unlimited self, the unconditioned self. Then my opportunities will be unlimited. Therefore I will have the unlimited happiness. Thats what we have learned so far in Bhagavad Gita. Now we are making a work plan. So right from the beginning of this chapter we have seen that Arjuna asked question about what is renunciation Tyaga.
From the overall discourse we have come to the conclusion that the only way to achieve the then Moksha, the liberation is by giving up things, not acquiring things by Tyaga and Sannyasa only. So Arjuna wanted to know what is the difference between the Tyaga and Sannyasa? And Bhagavan made it very clear in a very simple term that Karma Phala Tyaga is Tyaga. When I have no desire for particular result from my action, thats Dhyaga. And when I have no sense of agency, I have no desire for desire prompted actions, thats Sannyasa. When I give up the desire prompted action, its Sannyasa.
And then it seemed like Bhagavan is veering off on a tangent into a discussion about actions. It seemed like we started the discourse on Sannyasa and Tyaga, but now we are talking about action. In the last three verses we discussed what constitutes actions. There are five constituent parts of any action: Adhishtana, Karta, the organs of action, all the functions of the organs of action and perception,
and then the presiding deity -- the five elemental forces. These five have to come together for any action to come into existence. So if any one of them is missing, the action will not take place. So if the body is not there, there wont be any action. If ego is not there, there will not be any action also. So we have learned that action requires the five constituent parts.
And now well be talking about what is the anatomy of action. So the question is why Bhagavan is moving from discussion on sannyas and tyaga into actions. If you remember, in chapter four, after learning Sankhya Yoga and Karma Yoga, we talked of Gnana Karma Sannyasa Yoga. This sannyasa from the actions is only possible by knowledge about who is the actor, who is the doer. Right now the sannyas is not possible for me as long as Im identified with the doer.
If I think I am the doer, giving up action is not possible. Should I give up all the actions? As it seems that action is the root cause of all my problems. Action may be appropriate, inappropriate. It gives either a good, bad or somewhere in between result. Why not I get out of completely and say, well let me not act and therefore there wouldnt be any consequences.
By very nature that we are living entities, its not possible. We have learned that in previous chapters and in this chapter there is not even for a moment that we can stay without action. Nahi Kastchat Kshanama PI Jatu Tishtadhya Karma Krut. The signature of life is action. So as long as Im alive, Ill be acting. So giving up action is not the solution.
Then what is the solution? The solution is to renounce actions in knowledge. If I take ownership of my actions, then Im bound by my actions. It is more like filing bankruptcy. If I have a company and I have taken ownership of the company and I have done everything that is supposed to be done, and I end up with a huge debt. What is my out from there?
The American law says the only way you can get out of it, file for chapter 11. First you file for chapter 11. Say let me reorganize myself. So everything I have done right now is null and void. Nobody can come, no creditor come and ask for anything for me. And if that doesnt work out, I can reconstitute myself.
I file for complete bankruptcy. At that point, I disown everything that I owned in that company. Im no more responsible for the functioning of the company nor for the assets. Im not the owner of the assets and Im also not responsible for the debt. Now Im completely free and clear from that. Therefore, we have the limited liability companies.
We want to compartmentalize our responsibility. So Bhagavan said, you can do this. You can file for bankruptcy in your actions. If you disown your actions, if you say I am not the doer then you are not responsible for any of our actions. If I realize that I am not the doer -- the I which I consider I right now is actually the conditioned self, the conditioned ego that is identified with this body, mind and intellect, and therefore I feel responsible for it.
Well, if youre a doer, then as you have learned, out of the five constituent parts of the action, one is the Karta, the doer. That doer is as much involved in the action as the other four. So Bhagavan said, the only way to get out of it is to realize who the actor is. Which is what Gnana Karma Sannyasa is about. I, as an I without any superimposition on it. Superimposition is I am an architect.
Well, thats a superimposition on I. I am a father, another superimposition. I am a brother, another superimposition. If I remove all the superimpositions, what remains as I -- is that I really a doer? That is the I Im concerned about, the one that wants to be happy. So Bhagavan said that we need to understand what constitute actions. Then also now we have to understand where our misunderstanding is.
So from these previous verses we have concluded this action belongs to Prakriti, the manifest world. We also learned in chapter 13: Prakriti is the cause for Karya and Karana -- action and the instruments of action. But Purusha, Sukhadu Khana Boktrutvi Hetuhu Uchyate -- Purusha is the enjoyer of Sukha and Dukha. My nature, and the nature of the world of objects, creates this action.
Because I have a vasana for singing, I go to music concert. So this is the interaction between the world of objects and my vasanas. They are all part of this Prakriti. But I, the self is not really involved in it. I as an I has no vasanas, no conditioning. And therefore its not involved.
If I fail to recognize, Bhagavan said, then you are the doer. As an ego, youre fully involved and vested in that and you will bear the results of it. Tatra evam sati kartaram tmanam kevalam Tu yaha pashati akrut buddhihe. Whose Buddhi is not trained in thinking finer points about what is right and what is wrong, what is reality and what is non reality. Sa pasyati durma tehi. Such a persons mind is perverted.
Perverted in essence is not seeing the reality as it is and getting affected by the wrong notion of what reality is. Dhurma tehi akrad buddhi. Why these words are used? Because he says, because you are seeing. Tatyaam siddhi kartaram atmanam kevalam to yahu consider atma itself to the doer. One who sees that atma is the doer, hes wrong.
Because he does not have the finer intellect to realize what is right and wrong. Also he is influenced by wrong mati. His mind is tilted, polluted by vasanas, his intellect is clouded and therefore he does not see who the doer is. Because we elaborately analyzed and came to the conclusion that the action is only taking place in the realm of the Prakriti and the Purusha is not involved at all. The universal Purusha is not involved. We have used this example over and over again.
The space in this room is not participating in any activity of this room. But because we are identifying it with the walls, floor and ceiling, it becomes a room space. Now it is all the qualities of this room. Height, length, breadth; polluted air or clean air; light or darkness. All that is associated with this room is actually the conditioning superimposed in the space which was always here, is here and will always remain here. When you remove this building, the space will go back to its original condition.
But it was unpolluted, pristine space. That space is not taking part in any of the activity of this room. The same way, the self in me which enables me to do all these activities, when it is seen as unconditioned, is not taking any part in them. But it seems like its taking part, because Im identifying it with my mind, my intellect and my body. Now Im thinking that the conditioned self is the only self and that hes the doer.
That notion is wrong and therefore we are suffering. So this verse clearly says you need to differentiate between who is the doer and who are you. Are you the conditioned self, the ego? Or you are the unconditioned self, that which is imperishable, indestructible. Yasya na aham kruta bhavah buddhi Yasya na lipya de hatwh iman lokan hanti na ni badyade. So we are coming back to what we want to know.
How should I act in this life? He said, you act as you have to. Because once you understand that yasya naham kuta bhavaha once you realize that I, the self is not the doer, not taking any part in action, Im just a saxichaitanya. Im just the enabler. Welfare check comes to the person who is receiving welfare. That check will enable that person to go and buy whatever necessities he has.
What he buys is entirely up to that person. We have heard complaints about people on welfare. Use the welfare checks to go and buy beer or whatever, the alcohol versus buying food. But because that is according to him, welfare department only sends you a check, enables you to buy things in your grocery store. After that, it is entirely up to you how you use that. This life in me is enabling me to act.
But its not taking part into what field Im acting in. That comes from my vasanas, my mental makeup, my intellect capabilities in my body. Thats how I find my field. So Bhagavan said, yasya na aham kruta bhavah. One with his finer intellect came to the conclusion that I am not the doer. Such a person Buddhi Yasyana Lipyate whose intellect is not clouded by all the experiences of my life.
So right now my Buddhi is clouded by what I experienced. Experiences press on my mind, and that impression creates what I consider to be reality. So next time when I encounter the similar situation, Ill use that as a reference point and then act accordingly. Some people who start investing in one field get successful in first venture. He continues to do that and he has more positive attitude.
Next guy who does the same thing but fails the very first time, hell have a negative impression of what to do in that field.

These verses reveal the five causes that must combine for any action to occur: adhishthana (the body or seat of action), karta (the doer or ego), karana (the various instruments or sense organs), the diverse functions of these instruments, and daivam (destiny or the presiding cosmic forces). This teaching from Sankhya philosophy dissolves the illusion that I alone am the doer. Consider: if any one of these five factors is absent, the action cannot happen. If the body is not present, if the ego is not engaged, if the instruments are not functioning, if the circumstances do not align - the action simply will not occur. This means our individual contribution is just one-fifth of the equation.
The insight becomes even more liberating when we realize that these five causes apply equally to right and wrong actions, to actions of body, speech, and mind. The mechanism of action is neutral - it is our identification with it that creates bondage. Like understanding that electricity powers both the heater and the air conditioner without preference, understanding the mechanics of action helps us stop taking personal credit or blame for outcomes that depend on factors far beyond our control.
Reflect on a recent accomplishment you feel proud of. Now analyze: What was the role of your body and its health? What instruments and skills were involved? What circumstances had to align? What cosmic factors - timing, luck, the cooperation of others - contributed? Honestly assess how much was truly you versus the coming together of these five factors. This contemplation naturally reduces ego and opens the door to genuine humility and freedom from the burden of being the sole doer.
